framework.name: Field-to-Decision Transformation Framework
framework.thesis: Digital transformation succeeds when people, process and technology are designed together from the same goals and pain points, and every decision along the way is grounded in data that is fit for purpose.

cycle.detail: Start from the business objective and the operational KPIs that prove it. Agree what "better" means before choosing any tool.
Baseline the KPIs and the data behind them. Map goals and pain points for every stakeholder layer, from frontline crews to leadership.
Set the people strategy per layer, build the programme and SOPs from it, and select technology that fits the goal and the process.
Requirement, acceptance criterion and evidence for every capability, tested in real shift conditions and signed in the field.
Track data trust, adoption and realised value. Feed the results back into strategy and the next iteration.

pillars.name: Strategy & goals
pillars.question: What outcome must the operation deliver, and how will we know?
do: Translate the strategic objective into operational KPIs and data requirements (goal tree)
Agree targets and acceptance thresholds with the KPI owners
Prioritise use cases by value and feasibility

pillars.name: People
pillars.question: Who has to change, from operator to executive, and what will make them?
do: Identify goals and pain points for every stakeholder layer, from frontline crews to the site leadership
Map each group on power and interest (Mendelow) to set how closely it is engaged
Diagnose each group with ADKAR and act on the weakest element; Prosci / Kotter for the organisation-level change plan
Training, coaching and champions on every shift, including nights
Track adoption per group as a KPI, not a feeling

pillars.name: Process
pillars.question: What will people do differently on every shift, and who is accountable?
do: Build programmes, procedures and SOPs from the people strategy and from real field workflows
RACI with one accountable owner per decision
Management of change for tags, rules and thresholds
Shift handover and review routines that use the trust score
Retire the old report or spreadsheet on a fixed date

pillars.name: Technology
pillars.question: Which tool fits the goal and the process, and does it run at 3 AM?
do: Select and configure technology against the goal tree and the agreed process
Factory and field acceptance against criteria written with the users
A pipeline that delivers data on purpose, on time and relevant
24x7 run model with SLA, monitoring, incident management and MTTR

pillars.name: Data foundation
pillars.question: Is every decision, about the programme and in the operation, grounded in data we can trust?
do: Data for decisions: baselines, pain-point evidence and adoption telemetry steer the approach strategy
Data from technology: operational data that is fit for purpose, timely, relevant and reconciled
Quality measured per dimension, every day, with failures quarantined and owned

pillars.name: Governance
pillars.question: Who owns each dataset, KPI and decision, and how are conflicts resolved?
do: Data owners and stewards named for every dataset
Business glossary, lineage and system of record per KPI
Data governance council with decision rights and escalation path
Annual maturity assessment with improvement targets

pillars.name: Value realised
pillars.question: Did operational excellence improve, and does it add up to the strategic result?
do: Value statement per capability, recorded only after it shows in operations
Operational KPIs (uptime, tonnage, safety, cost) linked back to the goal tree
Lessons fed into the next cycle

fit_for_purpose.name: On purpose
fit_for_purpose.detail: Every dataset serves a named decision and a KPI with an owner.

fit_for_purpose.name: On time
fit_for_purpose.detail: Data lands inside its freshness SLA for the shift that needs it.

fit_for_purpose.name: Relevant
fit_for_purpose.detail: Right grain and scope for the decision, with no duplicates or out-of-scope rows.

fit_for_purpose.name: Trusted
fit_for_purpose.detail: Validated against rules and reconciled against an independent source.

playbook.title: Leadership asks for a dashboard next month
playbook.symptom: A solution is requested before the problem is defined.
playbook.signal: No baseline KPIs; data quality unknown.
playbook.root_cause: Technology is being chosen before goals and pain points are understood.
resolution: Run a two-week discovery: goal tree, pain points per stakeholder layer, baseline data quality
Show leadership the baseline trust score and what it means for the dashboard they asked for
Agree the first use case and its acceptance criteria, then build
playbook.example: Kestrel Gas Field started at a trust score near 70. A dashboard on that data would have shown confident but wrong allocation figures.

playbook.title: Rolling out a new system to shift crews
playbook.symptom: Four crews on a rotating roster, day and night, with different leaders.
playbook.signal: Adoption differs by crew and by shift.
playbook.root_cause: Training and support planned for day shift only.
resolution: Map each crew on power and interest and run ADKAR per group
One champion per crew; train at shift change, including nights
Update the shift handover SOP so the new system is the source used at handover
playbook.example: Ridgeback Pit dispatchers reached 88% adoption once each crew had its own champion.

playbook.title: An instrument reads with a systematic bias
playbook.symptom: Weighbridge tonnage consistently above on-board payload.
playbook.signal: WIM vs FMS gap around +4% for weeks, outside the 2% accuracy target.
playbook.root_cause: Loadcell calibration drift; no daily zero-check.
resolution: Calibrate with certified test weights and issue the certificate
Add a reconciliation rule against an independent source and a daily zero-check SOP
Show the before/after evidence to the people who stopped trusting the number
playbook.example: The WIM gap fell from about 4% to under 0.5%, and production reporting accepted WIM tonnage.

playbook.title: A data quality rule starts failing overnight
playbook.symptom: Quarantine rate on one source jumps at 02:00.
playbook.signal: Rule engine raises a data quality incident.
playbook.root_cause: An upstream change, such as a patch, tag remap or sensor fault.
resolution: Follow the runbook; confirm the field condition with the control room
Page the named steward and fix at source; never patch downstream
Mark affected KPIs "use with caution" on the shift report until a clean run
playbook.example: Historian tag quality failures after an OS patch were restored in about 3.5 hours.

playbook.title: The data is good but nobody uses it
playbook.root_cause: A people gap, usually Desire or Reinforcement. The old way still works, and no one asks for the new one.
resolution: Find the weakest ADKAR element per group
Involve users in defining the KPI they will be measured on
Supervisors use the new view in their reviews; retire the old report on a fixed date
playbook.example: Field supervisors lagged other groups until the trust score appeared on shift reports.

playbook.title: Everyone uses the data, but the data is wrong
playbook.symptom: High adoption, decisions made confidently on wrong numbers.
playbook.signal: Low trust, high adoption quadrant. The most dangerous state.
playbook.root_cause: No visible trust signal on KPIs; quality issues are invisible to users.
resolution: Show a trust badge on every KPI and downgrade it automatically when rules fail
Block regulatory or commercial use of a KPI until it is decision-grade
Communicate the fix and its evidence, so trust is restored rather than lost
playbook.example: Allocation figures reported to commercial teams while four wells exported pressure in bar.

playbook.title: The system is live but the spreadsheets come back
playbook.symptom: Shadow spreadsheets reappear a month after go-live.
playbook.signal: Manual entries outside the system; duplicate and late records rise.
playbook.root_cause: Technology delivered without a procedure, owner or retirement date for the old way.
resolution: Write the SOP with the crews who do the work and assign RACI
Set a date to retire the spreadsheet, then audit
Build the missing step into the form instead of tolerating a workaround
playbook.example: The daily report moved from a free-text spreadsheet to a validated form with a 10:00 deadline.

playbook.title: A powerful stakeholder is quietly against it
playbook.symptom: Support in meetings, budget or access withheld later.
playbook.signal: High power, low interest on the stakeholder map.
playbook.root_cause: The programme is not framed in their terms, such as compliance, cost or risk.
resolution: Keep satisfied: short briefs on the outcomes they care about
Involve them in acceptance criteria early
Escalate to the governance council if a decision is blocked
playbook.example: Hydrocarbon accounting engaged once reconciliation evidence was framed as month-end audit readiness.

playbook.title: Night shift loses connectivity
playbook.symptom: Pit radio drops; on-board units buffer and resync hours later.
playbook.signal: Late and duplicated cycles; night KPIs wrong at the 06:00 handover.
playbook.root_cause: The pipeline assumes data arrives in order and on time.
resolution: De-duplicate on resync and flag rows past the freshness SLA
Mark night KPIs "provisional" until sync completes
Handover SOP uses the provisional label instead of arguing the number
playbook.example: The OBU resync duplicate rule (MN-C-05) removed over-counted tonnage after radio dropouts.

playbook.title: Fewer false alarms must not mean less safety
playbook.symptom: Crews ignore fatigue alarms; tuning is proposed.
playbook.root_cause: Thresholds and hold times set without validated data.
resolution: Tune from six weeks of control-room-validated alerts (TP/FP)
Acceptance criterion of zero missed validated events over four weeks, with HSE sign-off
Share the evidence with operators to rebuild trust in the alarm
playbook.example: False alarms fell by about 20% with no loss of true-event coverage, and alarm adoption rose from 75% to 90%.

playbook.title: The vendor says it works; the field says it doesn't
playbook.symptom: Factory test passed, field acceptance failing.
playbook.signal: Capability stuck at the field acceptance gate.
playbook.root_cause: Acceptance criteria written without users or real shift conditions.
resolution: Rewrite criteria with the field, including night and wet-weather cases
Test in production conditions and collect evidence
Tie the payment milestone to field acceptance, not installation
playbook.example: Steward alerting is held at field acceptance until 20 injected failures are routed and closed.

playbook.title: Two systems disagree and both have an owner
playbook.symptom: Weighbridge and FMS give different tonnage; meetings argue the number.
playbook.root_cause: No system of record defined per KPI.
resolution: Define the system of record for each KPI in the glossary
Keep the other as an independent check through a reconciliation rule
Escalate unresolved conflicts to the data governance council
playbook.example: WIM became the system of record for reported tonnage, and FMS payload the operational check.

oil_gas.description: Onshore gas field, 12 producing wells, one fiscal export meter.

reconciliation.description: Sum of allocated well volumes must reconcile to the fiscal meter within 2%

interventions.title: Historian tag mapping & unit normalisation fixed at source
interventions.detail: Pressure tags on four wells were exporting in bar. Mapping corrected at the interface and a physical-envelope rule added.

interventions.title: Daily report moved to a validated digital form
interventions.detail: Free-text spreadsheet replaced with a form that enforces ranges and one record per well-day; entry deadline agreed with field supervisors.

interventions.title: Data owner and steward roles formally assigned
interventions.detail: RACI signed off by the asset manager. Every rule failure now routes to a named steward with a 24-hour response target.

mining.description: Open-pit coal mine, 40 haul trucks, one in-pit weigh-in-motion station.

reconciliation.description: WIM net weight must agree with FMS payload within 2% (accuracy class target)

interventions.title: WIM loadcell calibration to accuracy class
interventions.detail: Loadcells re-calibrated with certified test weights and a daily zero-check added. Systematic bias of about +4% removed.

interventions.title: Fatigue threshold and hold-time tuning
interventions.detail: Thresholds re-tuned from 6 weeks of validated alerts (TP/FP). False alarms down by 20% without losing true-event coverage.

interventions.title: Shift supervisor coaching on data-driven dispatch
interventions.detail: Supervisors trained to use the trust score before acting on a KPI. ADKAR reinforcement through a weekly toolbox talk.
